To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose an algorithm to reconstruct object shapes in 3D, from 2D object class labels, groundtruth figure-ground segmentation and 2D keypoint annotations, and show that it can be applied to one of the most popular object category detection datasets.
we have shown that it is possible to reconstruct object category datasets from their ground-truth labels, figure-ground segmentations, and a few keypoints.

we have developed a new approach for reconstructing object shapes from class labels and figure-ground annotations, and have demonstrated that our approach is able to produce plausible per-object 3d reconstructions for the PASCAL VOC dataset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of reconstructing object shapes in 3D from a single image.

the problem of popu- lating object category detection datasets (such as PASCAL VOC) with per-object 3-D reconstructions, using only the existing ground truth figure-ground annotations, and a small number of keypoint annotations per object.
how to generate 3D models from 2D images and how to apply the generated 3D models to object recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we are able to generate a large number of convincing 3D reconstrucitons from a single viewpoint for a variety of object classes, and that these reconstructions are of a high-enough quality to enable model-based recognition approaches.
our method produces 3D reconstrucitons of objects that are in the PASCAL dataset, but not in the PASCALLY dataset.
our method is capable of producing convincing per-object 2.5D reconstructions from a small set of 2D keypoint annotations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to provide dense, per-object, 3D reconstruction results on PASCAL VOC, and we believe that our results will be useful for the community.
our method provides a new way of looking at existing object detection datasets, and may help to re-stimulate model-based approaches in object recognition and scene understanding.
we have shown that it is possible to produce 3D object models for a large set of categories using only the 2D annotations available in the existing PASCAL VOC dataset.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PASCAL VOC dataset is not as "flat" as one might expect.
, even with very little supervision (e.g., 2D keypoints), it is possible to produce 3D object models that are sufficiently accurate to be useful for recognition.
it is possible to reconstruct 3D shapes of objects from 2D images, even when only loose class labels are available.
